---
title: "Geometry columns from DuckDB to sf"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_all <- requireNamespace("duckdb", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("DBI", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("qio", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = has_all)
```

A geometry column often starts in a database, is filtered and sorted
somewhere in the middle, and ends in sf for a map or a spatial join. Each
hand-off is a chance to lose something: digits when the column travels as
text, the coordinate reference system when a reader does not know where to
look for it, the meaning of an edge when a line on the sphere is read as a
straight one.

This article follows one column from DuckDB to sf and back, with zugeo
holding it in between. None of DuckDB, sf or qio is needed by zugeo; the
article uses all three.

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(zugeo)
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
invisible(DBI::dbExecute(con, "INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;"))
```

## From DuckDB, as GeoParquet

DuckDB writes a query result as GeoParquet, with the CRS in the file. Here
are ten thousand random points over Iberia, in WGS 84 longitude and
latitude.

```{r}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
invisible(DBI::dbExecute(con, "SELECT setseed(0.42)"))
invisible(DBI::dbExecute(con, sprintf("
  COPY (
    SELECT i AS id,
           ST_SetCRS(ST_Point(-9.5 + random() * 12.5, 36 + random() * 7.8),
                     'OGC:CRS84') AS geometry
    FROM range(10000) t(i)
  ) TO '%s' (FORMAT parquet, GEOPARQUET_VERSION 'BOTH')", path)))
```

`geo_parquet_info()` reads the footer and nothing else: the row count, the
encoding, the CRS DuckDB stored, and the box from the column's statistics.

```{r}
geo_parquet_info(path)
```

`geo_read_parquet()` gives a data frame whose geometry column is a
`geo_vctr`, its CRS taken from the file.

```{r}
df <- geo_read_parquet(path)
head(df, 3)
geo_crs(df$geometry)
```

## In zugeo

The column stays in Arrow memory. Its boxes, Hilbert keys and index are
computed over the coordinates. Sorting by Hilbert key puts nearby points
next to each other, which is what lets a reader skip a file's row groups.

```{r}
df <- df[geo_sort(df$geometry), ]
geo_box_all(df$geometry)
```

A packed R-tree answers "which points fall in this box", here a box around
Lisbon.

```{r}
tree <- geo_rtree(df$geometry)
lisbon <- geo_extent(-9.5, 38.5, -8.9, 39, crs = geo_crs(df$geometry))
near <- geo_query_box(tree, lisbon)
length(near)
```

## To sf

WKB is the bridge: `geo_as_wkb()` gives a list of raw vectors that sf reads
directly, and `geo_crs_text()` gives the CRS in a form PROJ reads.

```{r}
pts <- sf::st_sf(
  id = df$id[near],
  geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(
    unclass(geo_as_wkb(df$geometry[near])),
    crs = geo_crs_text(df$geometry)
  )
)
pts[1:3, ]
sf::st_crs(pts) == sf::st_crs("OGC:CRS84")
```

Nothing was rounded on the way. The coordinates sf holds are the doubles
DuckDB wrote, bit for bit.

```{r}
back <- geo_vctr(sf::st_as_binary(sf::st_geometry(pts)))
identical(geo_coords(back)[c("x", "y")], geo_coords(df$geometry[near])[c("x", "y")])
```

## And back to GeoParquet

A geometry column from sf comes back the same way, with its CRS given
explicitly, and goes out as GeoParquet 2.0. DuckDB reads it and finds the
same extent zugeo does.

```{r}
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
again <- data.frame(id = pts$id)
again$geometry <- geo_vctr(sf::st_as_binary(sf::st_geometry(pts)),
  crs = sf::st_crs(pts)$input
)
geo_write_parquet(again, out)
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, sprintf(paste(
  "SELECT count(*) AS n, min(ST_X(geometry)) AS xmin, max(ST_X(geometry)) AS xmax",
  "FROM '%s'"
), out))
geo_box_all(again$geometry)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```

## Where the guarantees stop

zugeo carries a CRS but does not interpret it: `geo_crs_equal()` compares
two without PROJ, and anything that needs a transformation is sf's or
PROJ's job. Lines with spherical edges are carried and written as
GeoParquet `GEOGRAPHY`, but a planar box or a planar Hilbert key of them is
refused unless asked for with `lossy`, because it can be wrong. And WKB
has no place for an edge type, so `geo_as_wkb()` on such lines is an error
by default: sf would read them as planar.
